Looking at the code of the `getResult` method in `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer`, it simply delegates the call to `optimizer.getResult()`, where `optimizer` is the underlying optimizer.

The `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer` class has a method `getOptima` that returns an array of optima values. This method throws an `IllegalStateException` if the `optima` array is `null`.

The bug in the `getResult` method of `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer` is likely related to how the `optima` values are managed and updated during optimization runs. If the `getResult` method simply returns the result of the last run of the underlying optimizer without considering the best result found among all runs, it explains why the result may not correspond to the best value.

To fix this issue, the `getResult` method in `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer` should be modified to return the best result found among all optimization runs rather than just the result of the last run.

The potential fix would involve updating the `getResult` method logic to consider all optima values stored during multiple optimization runs and return the best one.

Next, I will provide the suggested locations that should be fixed to address this issue.
The `org.apache.commons.math.optimization.MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer.getResult()` method should be fixed.

```java
org.apache.commons.math.optimization.MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer.getResult()
```
